title: Round 1: Normal year (tutorial)
special_event: A typical flood season. Try the controls and watch the meters.
teaching_note: A release below channel capacity is safe, and a longer high flow scours more riverbed. Real regulation events typically last about 20 days in June and July (Wang et al., 2017).

title: Round 2: Dry year, high demand
special_event: Little runoff and cities want water.
teaching_note: Flushing sediment uses water, so dry years force trade-offs. In 1997 the lower river was dry for 226 days at Lijin, which shows the cost of over-use.

title: Round 3: Wet year, high sediment
special_event: Plenty of water but a heavy sediment load.
teaching_note: Wet years give the most room to flush. In reality, the size of a regulation event depends largely on how much water is stored in the reservoirs beforehand.

title: Round 4: Flood alert
special_event: A large inflow peak is approaching (6,000 m³/s is a teaching assumption). Releasing too little is risky.
teaching_note: Safety needs both a release within channel capacity and empty storage to absorb the peak.

title: Round 5: Ecological flow rule
special_event: A new rule protects the delta.

policy_card.title: Ecological flow rule
policy_card.rule: The delta must receive at least 800 m³/s (teaching assumption, not an official target).

teaching_note: Environmental rules set a floor on releases. Real ecological-flow studies for Lijin use much lower base flows plus short pulse flows.

title: Round 6: Climate-reduced runoff
special_event: Runoff is lower than in the past.
teaching_note: Inflow to the middle reaches fell markedly from the 1990s. Planning has to adapt to less water and less sediment.

title: Round 7: Allocation quota, high sediment
special_event: A new quota protects water users.

policy_card.title: Allocation quota rule
policy_card.rule: At least 25% of water must be reserved for supply (teaching assumption).

teaching_note: Quotas guarantee supply but limit the water available for flushing. The real 1987 scheme shared about 37 billion m³ of roughly 58 billion m³ of runoff.

title: Round 8: Final test
special_event: Dry year, low storage, both policy rules active.
teaching_note: Earlier decisions carry over: the channel capacity and storage you left behind decide what is possible now.
